s1.syndrome_frame: Chronic ankle pain and swelling with bony lesion
salient_findings: Pain and swelling around the right ankle for 1 year
Bony thickening over the lateral malleolus
Submetaphyseal lytic lesion in the distal tibia with a well-defined sclerotic margin
key_facts: 13-year-old boy
1-year history of pain and swelling around the right ankle
Gradually increasing in size
Bony thickening over the lateral malleolus
Ankle and subtalar joints have a full range of motion
Complete blood count within normal limits
Erythrocyte sedimentation rate was 68 mm at the first hour
Submetaphyseal lytic lesion in the distal tibia with a well-defined sclerotic margin

shortlist.label: Brodie's abscess
shortlist.why_kept: Submetaphyseal lytic lesion with sclerotic margin and elevated erythrocyte sedimentation rate

shortlist.label: Osteomyelitis
shortlist.why_kept: Chronic pain and swelling with elevated erythrocyte sedimentation rate

shortlist.label: Ewing's sarcoma
shortlist.why_kept: Lytic lesion in the distal tibia with systemic symptoms

shortlist.label: Osteosarcoma
shortlist.why_kept: Lytic lesion in the distal tibia with bony thickening

shortlist.label: Chondroblastoma
shortlist.why_kept: Lytic lesion in the distal tibia with well-defined sclerotic margin

raw.rationale: The presence of a submetaphyseal lytic lesion with a well-defined sclerotic margin in the distal tibia, along with elevated erythrocyte sedimentation rate and normal complete blood count, is consistent with Brodie's abscess, a type of chronic osteomyelitis.

rejected.label: Osteomyelitis
rejected.why: While osteomyelitis is related to Brodie's abscess, the specific radiographic findings and clinical presentation point more directly to Brodie's abscess as the diagnosis.

rejected.label: Ewing's sarcoma
rejected.why: Ewing's sarcoma typically presents with more aggressive features, such as systemic symptoms and a permeative appearance on radiographs, which are not described in this case.

rejected.label: Osteosarcoma
rejected.why: Osteosarcoma usually presents with more pronounced bone destruction and formation, and the patient's age and lack of systemic symptoms make this less likely.

rejected.label: Chondroblastoma
rejected.why: Chondroblastoma is a rare tumor that typically occurs in the epiphyses of long bones, which does not match the submetaphyseal location described in this case.
